summary: Full audit of content/blog/09-apartment-utilities-cost.md completed. Page fails search-intent for 'apartment utilities cost' (Quick Answer delivers no number in ≤3 sentences). Table of state electricity averages is unverified (could not download EIA Table 5a this run). Zero internal links to related articles (11-kwh, 44-water, 16-budget-billing, state-average page). Missing aggregated total utility cost for apartments. Grade C-.
findings: Search-Intent Miss: Quick Answer does NOT contain a $/mo number. It says 'National cost tables cannot tell you what a specific apartment... will cost' — searchers wanting 'how much do apartment utilities cost' get no immediate answer. The two sentences: 'Build an apartment utility budget from the lease...' and 'Before signing, request a written explanation...' contain no cost figures.

Table sourcing vague: 'Source: EIA Electric Sales, Revenue & Average Price, Table 5a (latest 12-month period)' — no specific year stated. Monthly bill values (e.g. $164 CA, $167 TX) are calculated as rate × usage, not directly from EIA which provides average monthly bill directly.

Table figures UNVERIFIED: Could not download EIA Table 5a binary (xlsx/xls/PDF) from sandbox. EIA FAQ (https://www.eia.gov/tools/faqs/faq.php?id=97&t=3, retrieved 2026-08-29) reports national average 899 kWh/mo for all homes — California 542 kWh and Texas 1,172 kWh are plausible for state-level residential but cannot confirm exact values without the actual table.
No internal links found. grep for '11-kwh', '44-water', '16-budget', '2026-utility-cost-index-by-state' returned zero matches. Page has no cross-references to related utilityexplained articles.
No aggregated total utility cost. Page only provides electricity costs; no gas, water, internet, or all-utilities total. Searchers expecting 'apartment utilities total $X/mo' leave unsatisfied.

Renters-specific angles covered shallowly: RUBS and budget billing mentioned in checklist items but not elaborated. Claims like 'Most apartments include these in rent' (water/sewer/trash) are unsourced anecdotal — not verifiable.
Gas and water cost data absent entirely. No average gas bill or water bill for apartments — only electricity table. No EPA water figures sourced.
Hero flag already shipped (2026-08-28), hero_below_answer: true in frontmatter — the residual engagement defect is content/answer quality as suspected.
Title and meta description match voice but do not promise numbers: title 'How to Budget for Apartment Utilities', description avoids cost figures deliberately.
